ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no_action: the sole off-route segment is exempt under RD-4(a); no fare adjustment and no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered ride from Punggol Waterway Point to Tampines Mall, 12.40 km in 24.7 min, charged $29.26 against an estimate of 9.8 km / 15.1 min [F1][F2][F6]. Because it is metered, any unexempted detour kilometre would enter the fare, so RD-2 supplies the refund formula (unexempted extra_km × distance fare ÷ distance km) [F6][RD-2].

RD-1 requires each off-route segment in the record to be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5; here the record contains exactly one such segment, F3 (09:03–09:11, 3.97 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.80 km, +2.18 km, reaching 1040 m off the optimal route), and the trip-wide +2.6 km in F1 is not separately segmentable into any further detour [F1][F3][RD-1].

On that single segment the driver's account is not merely a statement: F8 (his post-trip claim of an accident on the Tampines Expressway) is corroborated by the traffic record. F12 records an Accident on the Tampines Expressway (towards PIE) after Punggol Road Exit, reported 08:44, located 0 m from the optimal route — i.e. on the very stretch that was replaced — and 08:44 precedes the segment start of 09:03 within the trip window 08:56–09:20; F9 adds that same expressway at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) during 08:47–09:03 [F8][F12][F9][F3][RD-4]. That satisfies RD-4(a)'s location and timing conditions, so F3 is the substituted stretch of the optimal route and the segment is exempt.

The rider's apportionment argument — that the incident window closes at 09:03 while the segment runs to 09:11, leaving the surplus 2.18 km unexempted [F9][F3] — is an inference, not a fact: no fact records a return to the optimal corridor at 09:03, the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and F9 is a speed-band fact which RD-4(b) says cannot exempt (or, here, partition) a segment on its own [F9][F3][RD-4]. The record therefore does not split F3 into an incident-covered part and a bare remainder, and I do not treat missing apportionment evidence as favouring the rider [F3][RD-2]. The alternate corridors' bands (F10 band 2, F11 band 4) are corroborative context only and are not relied on for the exemption [F10][F11][RD-4].

RD-5 gives the driver no shelter at all — F7 records no in-app messages, so there is no rider message before the segment agreeing to anything, and F8 is a statement, not consent [F7][F8][RD-5] — and D5/D9 on both sides concede there was no driver errand and no stop, so the segment rests on RD-4 alone [F3][RD-5].

With no unexempted segment, the RD-2 multiplicand is zero, and FARE-1 is not engaged: F6 shows waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 and no undisclosed add-on, and F5 shows surge 1.0× [F6][F5][RD-2][FARE-1]. RD-6's precondition also fails: F15 shows 0 route disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so no flag_account attaches [F15][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver statement F8 and the (empty) chat F7. The complaint is a fare/route grievance ("I never agreed to any change"), F8 is an explanation of the reroute, and there is no chat; nothing alleges threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous driving [F7][F8][F14], so safety_concern is none.

segment_findings.reason: The single off-route segment (09:03–09:11, 3.97 km against 1.80 km optimal, +2.18 km) replaces the stretch of the optimal route covered by an Accident on the Tampines Expressway reported 08:44 at 0 m from that route, before the segment start [F12][F8][F3]. RD-4(a)'s location and timing conditions are therefore met and the segment is exempt; RD-2 refund on it is zero [RD-4][RD-2]. The rider's 09:03 cut of the segment rests on a speed-band window which RD-4(b) says cannot exempt a segment alone, and no fact records the driven path's road names, so the record does not split the segment [F9][F3][RD-4].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the surplus 2.18 km of F3 is unexempted because the expressway incident window ends at 09:03 [F9][F3] is an inference from a speed-band fact; RD-4(b) states a band alone does not exempt a segment, and no fact records a return to the optimal corridor at 09:03 or the road names of the driven path [F9][F3][RD-4]. The record does not apportion F3, and the exemption under RD-4(a) stands on F12 [F12][RD-4].

The $3.07 refund (2.18 km × $1.4097/km from F4) presumes an unexempted segment; with F3 exempt under RD-4(a) because of F12, the RD-2 multiplicand is zero, so the amount is $0 and the outcome is no_action [F3][F4][F12][RD-2][RD-4].

Correct that F3 exists and is the only off-route segment under RD-1, but RD-1 makes a segment unexempted only if RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 fail, and F12 supplies the RD-4(a) exemption on that segment [F3][F12][RD-1][RD-4].

The driver's framing that the rider's $3.61 distance excess in F4 is the RD-2 cap is not applied: F4 measures 2.56 km of corridor-matched excess (F4 and F1 exceed F3's 2.18 km extra_km), whereas RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's own extra_km; here that figure is zero once F3 is exempt [F3][F4][F6][RD-2][RD-4].

Correct that no flag_account attaches (F15 shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so RD-6's precondition fails), but RD-6 is not the basis of the outcome; the ruling rests on the RD-4(a) exemption of F3 through F12 [F15][F3][F12][RD-6][RD-4].
